content.comment_body: I need to verify when real data is read from a converter using TCP Modbus to RS485. If the RS-485 connection fails, the [product_name] controller continues to show previous data and does not identify the communication error. A sample function has been added. I read data from the Modbus device into a register every 2 seconds; this data is cleared for 2 seconds before the next read from Modbus. A specific register indicates when data is freshly read from Modbus. If no Modbus read occurs after 5 seconds, the register is reset.

There might be alternative approaches depending on your Modbus device, but you have not specified its type. Is there a coil or register that reliably changes value in short intervals? For example, a coil could serve as a watchdog signal, updating every second, or a register could act as an internal counter, changing each second. If you have such a signal, monitor it in [product_name] controller for changes. If the value remains unchanged for more than 5 seconds, it indicates an error. Regards, [user_name]
My device is Altivar 61 and the converter is ET-485.
Do you expect me to search for manuals and resolve the issue? If you need help, please provide the component links and list the relevant order numbers.

analysis.insight_summary: The user highlights that when the RS-485 connection fails, the [product_name] controller continues to display outdated Modbus data, without flagging any communication errors. This leads to uncertainty about the reliability of the data presented, making it challenging to identify real-time connectivity issues using the existing [company_name] system.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants the [product_name] controller to accurately detect and indicate when real-time data from the Modbus-connected device is no longer being refreshed due to communication loss.
